page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported via AES flags. The instance provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and includes no GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory performance, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 3009.48, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Uncached large block read memory bandwidth reached 96.47 GB/sec, with write bandwidth measuring 44.25 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression ranked in the top 25 percent at 14.36 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression achieved 56.21 GB/sec. General compute metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1857.0) and multi-core (5966.0), as well as stress-ng compute tests, placed squarely in the middle 50 percent. Conversely, PassMark CPU tests recorded lower tiers, including a CPU score of 3947.59 and an encryption score of 751.5 in the bottom 10 percent, alongside reduced small-model LLM prompt processing speeds.

The r8gb.xlarge offers cost-efficient memory density per core, making it well-suited for RAM-intensive tasks that do not depend heavily on x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. Without bundled local disk storage, workloads must rely on network-attached storage or operate strictly in memory. Given the combination of high memory bandwidth, 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and consistent Redis performance of 9.2 million operations per second, this instance is suitable for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and general data processing services.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a 4-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz with dedicated physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration features 36 MB of L3 cache, an 8 Gbps network baseline, and AES encryption support, but lacks integrated local storage and GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional memory performance, achieving top-decile PassMark memory results and robust uncached read bandwidth of 96.47 GB/sec, while general CPU tests and LLM inference rank average to weak. It offers high memory density suited for in-memory caches, key-value stores like Redis, and data processing workloads.
